domain: border operations / queueing - service-standard exceedance nowcast at land ports of entry (Canada, federal)
prediction_question: For a measured CBSA land port of entry P, at instant T = the publication timestamp of one of CBSA's hourly border-wait-time snapshots, using only hourly snapshots of the archive with timestamps <= T (port identity, hour-of-day, day-of-week, season, recent wait history and status vocabulary), will the port's traveller flow exceed the CBSA highway-traveller service standard at ANY hourly snapshot in the next 24 hours, i.e. the window (T, T+24h]? A useful prediction lets a traveller or dispatcher re-time or re-route a crossing a day ahead, the same decision CBSA's own CanBorder app supports with forecasts; it also lets CBSA compare ports against its published 95% compliance target.
prediction_time: T = the snapshot hour of port P as printed in the archive's 'Updated' column (local-time string with a Canadian tz abbreviation; ADT/AST/EDT/EST/CDT/CST/MDT/MST/PDT/PST all measured in samples, each resolving to a fixed UTC offset; construction normalizes to UTC and states the offset table). Features are archive rows with Updated <= T. The target window (T, T+24h] is strictly after the instant; no part of it precedes T. RETROSPECTIVE, ARCHIVE-VINTAGE framing (recorded, not resolved to operational): the hourly archive is a frozen historical record published in batches (the 2010-2014 file and the 2014-2016Q1 quarterly files all carry CKAN created=2016-12-01; later quarters in batches 2017-03..2020-04; the series ends 2020-03-31 - Wayback capture 2021-11-23 shows 24 quarterly resources ending 2020-01..2020-03 and no successor, and the monthly service-standard file only appears by 2024-12), so the task claims no operational download availability at T; the files fetched today are one current vintage (the changelog documents FR translation fixes 2017-09-19 and a column rename 2016-07-20 as the only revisions; no EN data-value revision is documented, and current-vintage is the recorded assumption, same posture as the abs-visitor precedent). The self-collection option (hourly fetch of the live feed, ~3.3 KB per fetch, to build a fresh operational tail from now) is recorded as a possible extension, not part of this task.
target_definition: Binary: 1 if the port's Travellers Flow cell at ANY hourly snapshot in (T, T+24h] exceeds the CBSA highway-traveller service standard; 0 if no valid traveller cell in the window exceeds it. Label source: the Travellers Flow cells of the target window's snapshots; they are excluded from solver-visible features by a common-cutoff design (no shipped row may expose another scored row's outcome - the abs-visitor/canadabuys blind-join defect class is a named gate check). Threshold rule: the publisher's own service standard, whose documented forms are 10 minutes on weekdays (Mon-Thu) and 20 minutes on weekends (Fri-Sun) and holidays for FY2014-15..FY2017-18, and from FY2018-19 additionally 'July to August: 20 minutes (7 days a week)' (all quoted from CBSA service-standard pages, current and Wayback-pinned, see measurements.service_standard_evolution). Construction picks ONE of: (a) era-correct full rule (needs the FY2010-11..FY2013-14 forms verified - named prerequisite; FY2014-15 back is verified), or (b) the era-stable core rule 10/20 weekday/weekend-holiday everywhere (conservative, verified FY2014-15..present), or (c) a fixed plain threshold (e.g. >20 min) if the standard-linked rule proves unstable. Valid label denominator: traveller cells whose value is a minute count or 'No delay' (dictionary: 'No delay' = five minutes or less). 'Closed' (outside operating hours), 'Not applicable' (business line unavailable) and 'Missed entry' (no wait recorded) are not outcomes: an (office, hour) whose whole target window has no valid traveller cell is ineligible and right-censored out, never imputed; eligibility is decided from information at T (the port's own status history) not from the outcome. In-hour duplicate rows (publisher-acknowledged) are collapsed by a deterministic rule fixed before scoring: label = exceedance of ANY reported value in the (office, hour) group ('any' semantics; a conservative choice for a warning-use task, robust to the measured duplicate conflict pattern).

split_strategy: Temporal thirds on the frozen hourly archive 2010-01..2020-03, instant = snapshot hour; candidate windows train 2010-01..2016-12 / eval 2017-01..2018-12 / holdout 2019-01..2020-03 (each multi-year, disjoint, ordered; the 2020-03-21 COVID closure sits in the holdout's last 10 days and is a known-event fixture, not a whole-window effect). Clustering: (port, calendar-day) is the dependence unit (within-port serial correlation plus day-level demand shocks such as long weekends); clustered counts reported beside raw counts. Both classes expected in every window from measured per-port rates (12 ports with >30-min traveller exceedances in 2019 Q3 alone; 0 of 12 named busiest ports is all-negative), but exact per-window label counts at the chosen threshold rule are the FIRST construction measurement on the worker - the ~190 MB full archive is bulk work and stays off the coordinator; no sampled number is claimed as a total.

measurements.catalogue_2026_11_05: open.canada.ca CKAN package_search q='border wait': 4 datasets - Current BWT (d4a716f5, live CSVs only), Historical BWT Land (000fe5aa), Historical BWT Air (fe8020ad, monthly air-mode service-standard panel 31 KB - sibling noted, not opened), and an unrelated dataset. measurements.schema_and_vocabulary_2026_11_05: Archive columns: 'CBSA Office,Location,Updated,Commercial Flow,Travellers Flow' in the 2010-2014 file (header renamed 2016-07-20 per changelog) vs 'Custom Office Name,...' in 2019-era quarterlies; FR files are cp1252-encoded with French headers/values ('Nom du bureau', 'Aucun delay' family). Status vocabulary per the publisher's data dictionary (ref.odt v2017-04-11): minute counts; 'No delay' = five minutes or less; 'Closed' = outside operating hours; 'Not applicable' = business line not available at that port; 'Missed entry' = no wait recorded for the period. Case drifts by era ('No Delay' in the 2010-2014 file, 'No delay' in 2019); parse case-insensitively. All five behaviours measured in samples.
measurements.grain_and_coverage_2026_11_05: 2019 Q3 EN full quarter (81,836 rows, 26 offices, 2019-06-30 21:00..2019-10-01 01:00): 57,434 distinct (office,timestamp) keys vs ~57,564 theoretical office-hours for 26 offices x the quarter = 99.8% complete hourly grid. The archive's grain is (office, hour). Quarterly files OVERLAP at boundaries (Q3 starts 2019-06-30 21:00 before its nominal 2019-07-01; ends 2019-10-01 01:00; the 2010-2014 combined file contains rows into 2014-04-04, overlapping the first quarterly) - cross-file dedupe on (office, UTC-normalized hour) is mandatory. 2020 Q1 FR (80,439 rows, 26 offices, 2019-12-31 23:00 CST..2020-04-01 00:00 EDT) confirms the same grid at the archive's end.
measurements.duplicate_conflicts_2026_11_05: 2019 Q3: 11,960 of 57,434 (20.8%) office-hours carry >1 row; max 15; group-size distribution 2:139, 3:11494, 4:213, 5:38, 6:32, 7:26, 8:2, 9:4, 10:2, 11:9, 15:1; 18,053 rows sit in duplicate groups with CONFLICTING values (22% of all rows), concentrated at the six busiest ports (Peace Bridge 4,035; Queenston-Lewiston 3,861; Pacific Highway 3,802; Douglas/Peace Arch 2,383; Rainbow 2,279; Aldergrove 1,693) - the size-3 groups often carry three different values (e.g. Aldergrove 2019-06-30 21:00: 30/13/2), while large groups are mostly repetition with one differing value (Pacific Highway 2019-07-06 10:00: 14x'70' + 1x'44'). The publisher's changelog acknowledges exactly this ('duplicate records (same location and timestamp) ... with conflicting border wait time values'). Any-row ('any reported value exceeds') semantics is the recorded label choice; construction fixes and documents it before scoring.
measurements.base_rates_2019q3_2026_11_05: Traveller cells, 2019 Q3 (valid = minutes or no-delay = 80,630 of 81,836 rows; excluded: missed_entry 649, closed 557): minute-rows 30,390 (37.7% of valid) with mean 13.36 min, max 199. Per-cell exceedance: >5 min 22.6%, >10 min 14.6%, >15 min 10.1%, >30 min 3.79%, >60 min 0.75%. Per-port >30-min cells: Douglas/Peace Arch 1,212/3,318 (36.5%), Pacific Highway 803/4,687 (17.1%), Thousand Islands 106/338 (31.4%), St-Armand/Philipsburg 80/357 (22.4%), Aldergrove 224/2,401 (9.3%), Coutts 47/479 (9.8%), and 6 more ports positive; 2 of 25 ports with valid cells have zero >30 cells (small ports) - the exceedance population is concentrated but multi-port. Commercial flow exists at 23 of 26 offices in the quarter (not_applicable 14,987 rows) - a recorded optional variant, not the primary label.
measurements.known_event_fixture_2026_11_05: COVID-19 US-Canada border closure to non-essential travel 2020-03-21 (named event, expected verdict: traveller delays become rarer). Measured on the 2020 Q1 FR file: pre-2020-03-21 70,856 rows, no-delay 77.6%, minute-rows 14,360, max 298, >30-min 566 (3.9% of minute-rows); post-2020-03-21 9,583 rows, no-delay 87.3%, minute-rows 1,015, max 75, >30-min 18 (1.8% of minute-rows). Direction confirmed, magnitude moderate (not a collapse - essential travel continued and the archive ends 10 days after the event); recorded as measured, not inflated. Second fixture family: long weekends (Canada Day, Civic Holiday, Labour Day) at the BC and Niagara ports - per-window counts come from the worker pass.
measurements.service_standard_evolution_2026_11_05: Highway traveller service standard, publisher's own pages (current + Wayback): FY2014-15, FY2016-17, FY2017-18: '10 minutes on weekdays (Monday to Thursday); 20 minutes weekends (Friday, Saturday, Sunday) and holidays', target 95% (FY2014-15 result 97.1%). FY2018-19 onward: adds 'September to June:' prefix and 'July to August: 20 minutes (7 days a week)'. Current pages (FY2020-21..FY2026-27) keep that form; quoted results 99.35% (FY2020-21, pandemic), 94.97% (FY2024-25), 96.9% (FY2025-26). The FY2015-16 and FY2010-11..FY2013-14 forms were NOT found in this session - named verification prerequisite for the era-correct label rule (option (b) core 10/20 rule avoids the dependency).
measurements.monthly_cross_check_panel_2026_11_05: The publisher's own monthly aggregate (source 2): 26 ports x 79 months 2019-04..2025-10, 2,054 rows, 0 duplicates, pct-met range 59.03..100.00; base rates for a monthly miss label: <100 65.5%, <99 47.9%, <97 34.3%, <95 26.1%, <90 13.8% (recorded for the cross-check design; a monthly task was NOT opened - the panel is small, own-history-only, and its observed refresh is annual despite the 'Monthly' claim). Cross-check plan for qualification: for the 11 overlap months 2019-04..2020-03, the archive-derived monthly share of office-hours meeting the in-force rule must reproduce the published pct-met within a stated tolerance; disagreement names the rule form actually used by the publisher.
measurements.archive_end_evidence_2026_11_05: The hourly series definitively ended: Wayback capture 2021-11-23 of the dataset page shows the 24 quarterly resources ending 2020-01..2020-03 and NO successor resource; captures 2024-12-02 and 2025-01-17 show the monthly file at 'to 2024-10-31'; capture 2026-01-16 shows 'to 2025-10-31' (current); blob Last-Modified 2025-12-16. CKAN resource for the EN 2020 Q1 file is missing, but the file is live (HTTP 200, HEAD 2026-11-05) at the predictable URL - all 24 EN quarterly URLs measured 200.
measurements.fetch_cost_2026_11_05: Coordinator, anonymous HTTPS: 2019 Q3 EN 5,705,884 B and 2020 Q1 FR 6,383,740 B each in a few seconds; monthly file 80,693 B; live feed 3,270 B; three 60 KB range slices of the 71,369,535 B combined file; 24 HEAD requests. Full harvest (worker, one job): 24 EN quarterly files (~5.0-13.5 MB each) + the 71.4 MB combined file ~= 190 MB across ~25 GETs; same machine class as canadabuys's measured ~8 s per 45 MB => minutes-scale, single standard worker job. Timezone normalization: 10 tz abbreviations measured, all fixed-offset Canadian zones.
measurements.novelty_searches_2026_11_05: Hugging Face datasets API search 'border wait': 0 hits; 'border crossing': 5 hits, all US BTS monthly VOLUME mirrors or Africa logistics sets - none are wait-time series, none Canadian. Web search: no ML-ready dataset or benchmark on the CBSA series found. Adjacent prior art (models in papers, not shipped datasets): deep-learning crossing-delay prediction at the Niagara Frontier borders from researcher-collected Bluetooth data (US DOT report, rosap.ntl.bts.gov/view/dot/50534); Blue Water Bridge ISFC crossing-time regression (dot/86608); El Paso CV-data crossing-time estimation (Sage 2024); a 2026 multi-modal border-queue framework on SYNTHETIC data (arXiv 2608.27010). CBSA's own CanBorder app ships forecasted wait times as a product, not as data with splits. US-bound waits are a separate product (CBP bwt.cbp.gov / BTS), explicitly distinct from this Canada-bound series.

review: Five contracts at probe time: (1) Redistribution - SUPPORTED: OGL-Canada 2.0 on the publisher's own package record (ca-ogl-lgo), explicit copy/modify/publish/adapt/distribute grant incl. commercial use; class A; attribution statement required and carried to LICENSE.md. (2) Prediction timing - SUPPORTED WITH RECORDED SCOPE: instant = archive snapshot hour T, features = rows with Updated <= T, target window strictly after T, timezone table measured; the framing is RETROSPECTIVE/ARCHIVE-VINTAGE because the archive is frozen (ended 2020-03-31, successor evidence chain via Wayback) and was itself published in batches - no operational-download claim is made, current-vintage assumption recorded (abs precedent posture). (3) Target - SUPPORTED: label source = Travellers Flow cells after T, excludable via common-cutoff design (abs-visitor defect class named as a gate check); the threshold has external meaning from the publisher's documented service standard (rule forms pinned FY2014-15..present via the publisher's pages incl. Wayback); eligibility and censoring defined at the instant (Closed/Not applicable/Missed entry are statuses, not outcomes); publisher-acknowledged duplicate conflicts measured (20.8% of office-hours) with a deterministic any-row rule fixed before scoring. (4) Split capacity - PARTIALLY MEASURED: grain and per-cell base rates measured on two full quarters (2019 Q3 EN + 2020 Q1 FR) + three era slices; three disjoint multi-year windows fit the 2010-2020 span with both classes expected; exact per-window counts need one bulk worker pass (recorded as the prerequisite to ready; never extrapolated to a claimed total). (5) Not a mirror - differentiated (novelty check recorded): no ML-ready task on the CBSA series anywhere found; closest prior art is researcher-collected-sensor models at 4-6 ports and CBSA's own app forecasts - neither ships data, splits or a scored contract; the nearest bench family abs-visitor-arrivals-direction is a monthly aggregate direction task on a different publisher/population, and its known defect class is addressed here by design.
next_action: One bounded worker measurement pass (advancement owns it), then ready/drop decision on measured criteria. Job: fetch all 24 EN quarterly files + the 2010-2014 combined file (~190 MB), sha256-pin each, normalize the Updated column to UTC, dedupe cross-file overlaps on (office, UTC hour), collapse in-hour duplicates with the any-row rule, and compute: (a) exact coverage (first/last timestamps, per-era office lists, office-hour grid completeness), (b) per-window (train 2010-01..2016-12 / eval 2017-01..2018-12 / holdout 2019-01..2020-03) eligible office-hours and label counts at the core 10/20 rule AND at a fixed >20-min threshold, with (port, day) clustered counts, (c) duplicate-conflict rate per era, (d) the 2019-04..2020-03 monthly pct-met cross-check against the publisher's monthly file under candidate rule forms. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA to flip ready: every window carries both classes with >=1,000 clustered positives at the chosen threshold, grid completeness >=95% of office-hours in every window, and a monthly cross-check that reproduces the published pct-met under exactly one candidate rule form (or a documented disagreement). FAILURE MODES to record instead: any window below those counts (choose a different threshold or drop), or a cross-check that no rule form reproduces (label meaning becomes unverifiable - drop or redesign on the fixed-threshold label with the disagreement recorded). If ready: construction step = the same worker job extends to the full artifact build (features from snapshots <= T only, target window rows never shipped to the solver, statuses and calendar features shipped, Closed/Not-applicable censoring), expected artifact = train/eval/holdout CSVs + quality.json with evaluation_contract under the repository's construction path, decided by the standard gate -> exact-byte acceptance -> reference scoring in that order.

novelty_check.theirs: The publisher (CBSA) ships the raw archive, a live current-only feed, and CanBorder app forecasts (a product, not data with splits); academic prior art predicts crossing delay at 4-6 US-border ports from researcher-collected Bluetooth/connected-vehicle sensor data (US DOT 50534 Niagara Frontier deep-learning study, US DOT 86608 Blue Water Bridge ISFC regression, Sage 2024 El Paso CV study) with no shipped dataset; a 2026 arXiv framework (2608.27010) uses synthetic data; US-bound wait times are a separate CBP/BTS product; Hugging Face search returns only US BTS monthly volume mirrors; no public dataset, splits or scored task exists on the CBSA series.
novelty_check.ours: First ML-ready public prediction task on the CBSA's own Canada-bound hourly border-wait archive (26 ports, 2010-01..2020-03, ~2.3M office-hours): reproducible construction from the official OGL-Canada series, temporal splits with a common-cutoff design against cross-row self-answering, censoring semantics for the published status vocabulary (Closed/Not applicable/Missed entry), a deterministic any-row rule for the publisher-acknowledged duplicate conflicts, and a label threshold tied to the publisher's documented service standard with the publisher's own monthly aggregate as a built-in cross-check.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
